name: How do I know if my luxury home design is over-customized?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my Los Angeles luxury home is becoming too customized to resell easily?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell if my Los Angeles luxury home is becoming too customized to resell easily?

acceptedAnswer.text: A luxury home becomes over-customized when too many decisions are made for a very specific owner profile rather than for the property itself. That can include unusual room layouts, highly niche finishes, or specialty spaces that are expensive to convert later. In Los Angeles, some customization is expected, but the design should still support broad usability and resale appeal. One way to evaluate this is to ask whether the feature improves daily life, whether it is easy to maintain, and whether a future buyer would see value in it. Timeless materials, flexible rooms, and strong proportions usually age better than trend-driven choices. The goal is not to make the home generic. The goal is to make it distinctive in a way that still feels believable, functional, and marketable over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: A home may be over-customized if the finishes, layouts, or features are highly specific to one lifestyle and would be expensive to change later. Strong luxury design balances personal preferences with timeless materials, practical layouts, and broad market appeal so the home still feels special without becoming difficult to resell.
